page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-64-lssd is a memory-optimized server instance from the c4d family. It features 64 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9B45 processor with x86_64 architecture, containing 32 physical cores with a thread-per-core ratio of 2.0. The system is equipped with 504.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.88 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance includes 2172 GB of NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 6 local SSDs. No GPU accelerators are present on this server type, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the AMD EPYC processor delivers top-tier single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3449.09 and a PassMark CPU score of 91421.05, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Multi-core performance is strong, registering 109864.8 in stress-ng multi-core tests. The memory subsystem demonstrates strong throughput, with a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 6631.63 GB/sec and uncached large block read and write speeds of 203.23 GB/sec and 129.23 GB/sec, respectively. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression both achieve top-tier status, processing at 37.63 GB/sec and 16.9 GB/sec.

The combination of high memory density, dedicated CPU allocation, and local NVMe SSD storage makes this instance suitable for database operations, which scored in the top 10% on PassMark with 39499.25 operations. Redis SET operations reached 110.03 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput was recorded at 71.98 GB/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of 504.0 GB RAM paired with 2.1 TB of local NVMe storage provides a consolidated platform for memory-intensive and I/O-heavy workloads, reducing the need for external storage attachments. Appropriate workloads include large-scale databases, in-memory caching layers, and high-throughput web serving.
